The Story Begins

Splitwise had a trust problem.

It started simply: a Bangalore flatmate opens Splitwise to log the month's groceries — only to hit a paywall after three entries. She switches to a WhatsApp note. Her landlord doesn't have the app. Her Goa trip group uses different apps. Every workaround chips away at Splitwise's core promise: make shared money simple.

🔒

Paywall Friction

Core features locked at 3–5 free entries/day. Users felt ambushed mid-task, leading to resentment and abandonment.

👥

The Non-User Problem

Landlords, occasional trip friends, non-app users — everyone had to have an account. Real life doesn't work that way.

🧩

Fragmented Experience

Groups buried alphabetically. "Settle Up" didn't log payments. Debt simplification created circular confusion.

"Splitwise should make my life easier, not harder. I need it to manage all my group expenses in one place without pushing me to pay for basics."
— Pragya, Marketing Associate, Bangalore · Persona from primary research
Chapter 2 — Research

We listened before we designed.

Three layers of research shaped every design decision: competitive benchmarking, a 30+ person survey, and 1:1 interviews — all pointing to the same root cause.

1

Secondary Research & Competitive Analysis

Benchmarked Tricount, Splid, Settle Up, Google Pay, Venmo — mapping strengths, pricing models, and UX gaps to find where Splitwise fell behind and where it could lead.

2

App Store Deep-Dive & User Reviews

Scraped and synthesised user reviews across platforms. Key theme: "perceived value doesn't match cost." Users compared Splitwise unfavourably to free competitors like Tricount.

3

Primary Survey + Questionnaire (30+ participants)

Students and young professionals in metro cities. Questions focused on pain points, non-user situations, and the one feature that could change everything.

4

1:1 Interviews & Heuristic Evaluation

Two in-depth user interviews (Pragya & Vasu) uncovered nuanced frustrations: circular debt confusion, leaving the app to pay, and the cognitive load of managing 8+ groups.

8+ users flagged

Non-User Exclusion

Landlords, trip companions who don't use Splitwise — there was no way to include them. Users resorted to manual calculations outside the app entirely.

7+ users complained

Daily Entry Limits

The free plan cap of 3–5 entries/day was a deal-breaker for frequent group activity. Named by Ashwika, Subrat, Aditya, Bhumika — and many more.

6+ requests

No UPI / In-App Payment

Users had to leave Splitwise to actually pay, then manually return to mark as settled. The Settle Up flow was incomplete by design.

Navigation

Groups Buried Alphabetically

Active groups — a Goa trip, this month's rent — sat buried among inactive ones. Users spent time searching instead of acting.

"I just want the app to handle the math, include friends who don't use it, and give me a dashboard I can trust without having to pay for every little thing."
— Vasu Acharya, Engineer, Bangalore · Primary research participant

Original Splitwise screens — annotated with core usability issues discovered during heuristic evaluation

The Diagnosis

One root cause. Four failure modes.

A 5 Whys analysis traced every friction back to a single design philosophy: Splitwise overemphasised expense logging while neglecting navigation, settlement clarity, and inclusivity.

Problem Statement

Splitwise struggles to deliver on its promise of being a simple, universal expense-sharing tool. Users face confusion in debt simplification, limited categorisation for meaningful insights, and the inability to seamlessly include non-users. Settlement flows lack integration and transparency, forcing users to rely on external apps. The app's overemphasis on basic logging while neglecting inclusivity, navigation, and clarity creates frustration, reduces trust, and ultimately pushes users away.

Chapter 3 — The Design

Four features. One coherent system.

The redesign addresses the four highest-priority gaps head-on — building each feature from user flows through to final screens.

Feature 01

Smart Dashboard — The Unified Hub

A single, clutter-free dashboard shows all active groups, recent expenses, pending balances, and a "Wallet Mood" balance summary in one scrollable view. Groups ranked by recent activity with pin support. No more hunting.

The "Your Week in Review" panel surfaces streak data, shared meals, and active trips — turning a transactional tool into something that feels alive.

Concept 1 — Desktop Dashboard

Feature 02

Pay Via UPI — Settlement That Actually Settles

The new Pay Via UPI integration closes the loop. Users tap once, choose PhonePe / GPay / Paytm, complete the transaction — and Splitwise auto-syncs the settlement back. No more manual "mark as paid."

User Flow — Pay Via UPI Integration

Feature 03

Guest Mode — No App? No Problem.

Placeholder accounts for landlords, occasional trip friends, or anyone who won't install an app. A link arrives via SMS or WhatsApp. Guests access a limited dashboard in their browser — see their share, pay via UPI. No account required.

Guest Mode — Tablet view showing expense breakdown and Pay via UPI

Feature 04

Analytics — Spending That Tells a Story

Full Analytics screen with spending trends, category breakdown (Food & Dining, Transportation, Entertainment), and monthly comparisons. Finally, the "why" behind the numbers — across all three devices.

Concept 1 — Desktop Analytics Screen

Chapter 6 — Impact

What this redesign changes — for real.

This isn't just a visual refresh. Each design decision directly addresses a measured user pain point. Here's what changes when the redesign ships.

8+
Users blocked by non-app exclusion — now solved with Guest Mode
0
Manual steps needed to log a UPI payment — auto-synced
↑ 3×
Faster access to active groups via activity-first sorting
100%
Of core flows — add, split, settle — available without premium
🏠

Flatmates & Roommates

Rent, groceries, utilities — all tracked in one place. No more daily entry caps cutting off mid-month. The dashboard shows a live wallet mood so everyone's on the same page without a single message.

✈️

Trip Groups

Goa trip with 8 people? Half of them don't use Splitwise? Guest Mode solves this entirely. Send a link, they see their share, pay via UPI — all settled before the flight home.

💡

Financial Awareness

The Analytics screen transforms raw debt numbers into spending stories. Users see where money goes — Food & Dining, Transportation, Entertainment — weekly and monthly, exportable in one tap.

🤝

Restored Trust

The #1 reason users left: feeling cheated by paywalls. By moving limits away from core flows, Splitwise earns trust back — and users who trust the app are the users who upgrade to Pro willingly.

⚡

Reduced Cognitive Load

Active-first group sorting, pinning, and a unified dashboard mean users reach their goal in fewer taps. Less time navigating, more time living — which is what expense apps are supposed to enable.

📊

Better Business Outcomes

Fair monetisation — Trip Pass, flexible day passes — means users pay for what they need, when they need it. This model converts more users than a blanket subscription wall ever could.

"Good design doesn't just solve problems — it removes the friction that stops people from living the way they want to. This redesign gives Splitwise back to its users."
— Design Brief, Splitwise Redesign Project · Kanishka Saxena, 2025
